questions.q: What does Honegger mean by imperfect courage?
a: Acting despite fear, even when your courage feels weak
Waiting for confidence before you take a big step
Taking only risks you can fully control
Pretending to be fearless so others follow you
questions.why: Lesson 1 says weak courage beats none, and small steps outside your comfort zone change your life.

questions.q: Which risks does Honegger count as fearless living?
a: Pursuing an adoption she could not yet afford
Rushing into a burning building to save a pet
Quitting her job without any savings
Investing her savings in a friend's business
questions.why: Lesson 1 says fearless did not mean heroics, but adoption without the money and selling jewelry at home.

questions.q: Why does vulnerability help in business, according to Honegger?
a: People relate to openness and trust you more
It lets you avoid answering hard questions
It proves you have nothing left to lose
It keeps competitors from learning your plans
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the more open she became, the more people connected with her and her business grew.

questions.q: What does the summary say about trying to do everything?
a: Small actions still matter, so just start with something
Wait until you can make a grand contribution
Focus only on problems close to your home
Leave large causes to governments and charities
questions.why: Lesson 3 quotes that little people doing little things everywhere can change the world.

questions.q: What was Honegger's business, Noonday Collection, built around?
a: Selling jewelry made by women in Uganda
Running leadership retreats for executives
Publishing guides for adoptive parents
Importing coffee from small farms
questions.why: The overview describes her helping Ugandan women sell their jewelry, which grew into the company.
